info.what: Flags inline <svg> elements that are exposed to screen readers but lack an accessible name.
info.why: Screen readers will read out raw SVG code nodes or ignore the graphic entirely. If it's decorative, it must be explicitly hidden. If it's informative, it must be named. WCAG 1.1.1: Non-text Content
info.fix: If the SVG conveys meaning, add aria-label="description" or a nested <title id="desc"> referenced by aria-labelledby="desc". If the SVG is purely decorative, add aria-hidden="true" to hide it from screen readers.

info.what: Flags <img> elements completely lacking an alt attribute, and explicitly separates 1x1 tracking pixels.
info.why: Screen readers will read the raw image filename or URL if the alt attribute is missing. For hidden tracking pixels, this results in a highly disruptive announcement of a massive tracking URL. WCAG 1.1.1: Non-text Content
info.fix: Add an alt attribute. For content images, provide a brief description. For tracking pixels and decorative images, provide an empty alt="" attribute or add aria-hidden="true" to the container.

info.what: Flags alt attributes containing unnecessary prefixes like 'image of' or 'photo of'.
info.why: Screen readers automatically announce the element as an image. Including these words forces the user to hear 'Image, image of...' redundantly. WCAG 1.1.1: Non-text Content
info.fix: Remove the words 'image of', 'picture of', or 'photo of' from the alt attribute. Just describe the subject directly.
info.detection_note: Matches the English words image, img, photo, picture and graphic anywhere in the alt text. Legitimate descriptions that use those words can be reported, and other languages are missed.

info.what: Flags <a> tags lacking readable text or accessible ARIA names.
info.why: Screen readers will default to reading the raw URL path out loud, which is often confusing and excessively long. WCAG 2.4.4: Link Purpose (In Context)
info.fix: Provide visible inner text for the link. If the link only contains an icon, add an aria-label or visually hidden text (e.g., <span class="sr-only">) describing the destination.

info.what: Flags anchor tags that lack actual routing destinations and are missing role='button'.
info.why: Using links to trigger JS actions confuses screen readers. A user expects a link to navigate them to a new page. If it executes a script or toggles a menu, it should be a Button. WCAG 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value
info.fix: If the element performs an on-page action (like opening a modal or submitting data), convert it to a <button> element. If you must use an anchor tag, add role="button".
info.detection_note: Only detects links whose href is '#' or starts with 'javascript:'. Fake buttons built in other ways are not found.

info.what: Flags ambiguous link text (e.g., 'Click Here', 'Read More') using exact word boundaries.
info.why: Users navigating via an isolated 'Links List' will lack context for where the destination actually leads. WCAG 2.4.4: Link Purpose
info.fix: Rewrite the link text to clearly describe the destination. Instead of 'Click here', use 'Read our annual report' or 'View full article'.
info.detection_note: Matches a fixed list of English phrases (click here, read more, learn more, more, link, here). Other languages and other vague wording are not found, and a longer link text containing one of these words can match.

info.what: Flags form controls missing a linked <label for>, an aria-label, or a direct <label> wrapper.
info.why: Screen readers cannot announce what the input is for. The user will focus the field and only hear 'Edit text', with no context. WCAG 3.3.2: Labels or Instructions
info.fix: Add a <label for="input-id"> that targets the input's ID, nest the input directly inside a <label>, or provide a descriptive aria-label.

info.what: Flags buttons with no internal text, missing an aria-label, or lacking a child image with an alt attribute.
info.why: Screen readers will only announce 'Button', providing zero context about what clicking the button will actually do. WCAG 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value
info.fix: Provide visible text inside the button. If the button only uses an icon, add an aria-label="Action Description".

info.what: Flags inputs relying solely on the placeholder attribute for their accessible name.
info.why: Placeholders disappear when a user begins typing, removing the instructions. Furthermore, default placeholder colors frequently fail text contrast minimums. WCAG 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value
info.fix: Provide a persistent, programmatic label (like a <label for="id"> or aria-label) instead of relying solely on the placeholder.
info.detection_note: Checks for a label[for] and ARIA names only. Other valid ways of naming a field are not considered.

info.what: Flags generic elements with onclick handlers lacking a tabindex and a valid semantic role.
info.why: Keyboard users cannot tab to or activate these elements. If an element behaves like a button, it must be programmatically focusable. WCAG 2.1.1: Keyboard
info.fix: Change the element to a native <button>. If a custom element is strictly required, add tabindex="0", a valid ARIA role like role="button", and ensure you handle standard keyboard events (Enter/Space).
info.detection_note: Only finds div, span and section elements with an onclick attribute. Click handlers attached in JavaScript (addEventListener, frameworks) cannot be seen, so an empty result does not prove there are none.

info.what: Scans the DOM for multiple elements sharing the identical id attribute. It uniquely tracks and categorizes hidden vs. visible duplicates in the DevTools list.
info.why: Screen readers and label mappings will only find the first ID. If multiple elements share an ID (even if one is hidden for mobile/desktop layouts), <label for> and ARIA reference attributes will fail to connect to the subsequent elements. WCAG 1.3.1: Info and Relationships
info.fix: Ensure every id on the page is entirely unique. If components are reused in multiple layouts, append a dynamic layout suffix to the IDs.

info.what: Validates that any ID referenced by an ARIA relationship attribute actually exists in the DOM.
info.why: A broken reference means the relationship is completely lost. The screen reader will not announce the label, description, or target widget if the ID does not physically exist. WCAG 1.3.1: Info and Relationships
info.fix: Ensure the ID string declared in the ARIA attribute exactly matches the id of an existing element currently present in the DOM.

info.what: Traverses the DOM to calculate the effective mathematical contrast ratio between visible text and its solid backing container. Dynamically evaluates font-size and font-weight against WCAG large-text thresholds.
info.why: Low contrast prevents users with visual impairments from reading content. Background images, complex gradients, or transparent floats are safely flagged for Manual Review to prevent false automated calculations. WCAG 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum) WCAG 1.4.6: Contrast (Enhanced)
info.fix: Increase the contrast ratio between the text and background color. Normal text requires 4.5:1 (AA) or 7.0:1 (AAA). Large text (18pt+, or 14pt+ bold) requires 3.0:1 (AA) or 4.5:1 (AAA).
info.detection_note: Colors are computed, but text over images or gradients cannot be decided and is flagged for manual review. Overlapping elements are not modelled.

info.what: Maps the standard, sequential H1-H6 heading structure.
info.why: Verifies the logical outline of the page. WCAG 1.3.1: Info and Relationships
info.fix: Ensure heading tags accurately represent the visual and semantic hierarchy of the content section they introduce.

info.what: Maps native HTML5 (e.g., <main>, <nav>) and ARIA (e.g., role='banner') structural landmark containers.
info.why: Allows screen reader users to jump quickly between core page sections via the Rotor or Shortcut lists. WCAG 2.4.1: Bypass Blocks
info.fix: Verify that all top-level content on the page is contained within at least one valid landmark region (e.g., main, nav, footer) so no content is orphaned.

info.what: Maps unordered (<ul>), ordered (<ol>), and glossary lists (<dl>) along with their children.
info.why: Ensures related items are programmatically grouped so screen readers can announce list sizes correctly. WCAG 1.3.1: Info and Relationships
info.fix: Verify that list containers (ul, ol) only contain valid direct children (li, script, template) and are not used purely for visual indentation.

info.what: Maps the root document lang declaration alongside any mid-page inline phonetic shifts.
info.why: Screen readers rely on the language tag to load the correct dictionary, accent, and pronunciation rules. WCAG 3.1.1: Language of Page WCAG 3.1.2: Language of Parts
info.fix: Ensure a valid ISO language code (e.g., lang="en" or lang="fr-CA") is defined on the root HTML element, and wrap any foreign phrases in inline spans with the respective lang attribute.

info.what: Extracts and visually prints the alt text directly over all <img> elements, and explicitly segregates 1x1 tracking pixels.
info.why: Allows rapid visual auditing of alternative text descriptions without needing to inspect the DOM manually. WCAG 1.1.1: Non-text Content
info.fix: Review the visually printed text. Ensure active images accurately describe their content or destination, and decorative layout/tracking images correctly use empty alt text (alt="").

info.what: Highlights all tabindex variations (0, -1, and > 0) simultaneously on the page.
info.why: Provides a sweeping visual map of the programmatic focus strategy. Allows auditors to ensure programmatic focus control is being routed correctly. WCAG 2.4.3: Focus Order
info.fix: Review positive tabindexes (red flags). Remove them if they improperly override the natural DOM reading order. Review negative tabindexes to ensure active components haven't accidentally been removed from the keyboard flow.

info.what: Traces the sequential path of focusable elements and flags traps. Main page elements are numbered sequentially (#1, #2). When focus enters an iframe, elements are marked with an [Iframe] tag and a hierarchical decimal (e.g., #4.1 indicates the 1st focusable element inside the 4th tab stop). Nested iframes add further decimals (e.g., [Nested] #4.2.1).
info.why: Simulates the exact path of the TAB key. Ensures logical flow and visualizes deeply nested cross-frame boundaries. WCAG 2.4.3: Focus Order
info.fix: Review the drawn path line for logical sequential flow (left-to-right, top-to-bottom). Verify that elements flagged as 'Focusable in Aria-Hidden' are safely deactivated (using inert or tabindex="-1") when their parent layer is closed.
info.detection_note: Simulated from tabindex, DOM order and frame structure. It does not press Tab, so scripted focus changes are not reflected.

info.what: Maps all elements utilizing an explicit role definition.
info.why: Allows rapid structural auditing of custom widget semantics. WCAG 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value
info.fix: Verify that the declared ARIA role exactly matches the design pattern and behavior of the component (e.g., using role="tablist" for a set of tabs).

info.what: Computes the final accessible name by simulating the browser's fallback calculation sequence: aria-labelledby, then aria-label, then native linked labels or inner text, and finally the title attribute.
info.why: Reveals exactly what a screen reader will announce. Identifies mismatching accessible names and dangerously silent controls. WCAG 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value
info.fix: Review the visually printed text. Ensure active controls missing a name (red flags) are properly labeled using visible text or an aria-label.
info.detection_note: Simulates the browser's name fallback order (aria-labelledby, aria-label, labels and text, title). It approximates the browser's accessible name algorithm.

info.what: Identifies supplemental instructional text linked to inputs via aria-describedby or title.
info.why: Ensures extended hints or error messages are programmatically tied to inputs so screen readers read them alongside the main label. WCAG 3.3.2: Labels or Instructions
info.fix: Ensure the ID declared in aria-describedby connects to a valid, visually persistent element that correctly describes the constraints or errors associated with the input.

info.what: Highlights elements utilizing aria-controls to dictate visibility of remote elements.
info.why: Links trigger mechanisms to their remote targets within the accessibility tree. WCAG 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value
info.fix: Verify that the referenced ID correctly maps to the container whose visibility or state is directly manipulated by interacting with this element.

info.what: Maps dynamic aria-live injection containers (polite, assertive).
info.why: Ensures dynamic content updates are announced to screen readers without requiring focus. WCAG 4.1.3: Status Messages
info.fix: Ensure the region exists in the DOM on initial load before dynamic content is injected into it. Use aria-live="polite" for most notifications to avoid interrupting the user.

info.what: Maps expandable widgets by their aria-expanded status, color-coded by true/false state.
info.why: Visualizes the current programmatic state of dynamic accordions and menus for easy testing. WCAG 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value
info.fix: Ensure JavaScript actively toggles this attribute between true and false in tandem with the visual display of the controlled content.

info.what: Maps toggle buttons by their aria-pressed status.
info.why: Visualizes the current programmatic state of toggle buttons (e.g., Mute/Unmute, Play/Pause) for easy testing. WCAG 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value
info.fix: Ensure JavaScript toggles this attribute when the button is activated. Do not use aria-pressed on elements that do not maintain a toggle state (like standard links).

info.what: Highlights elements that trigger interactive popup overlays (menus, dialogs, listboxes).
info.why: Prepares users for a context shift. Tells screen reader users that activating the element will spawn an overlay. WCAG 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value
info.fix: Verify that the attribute value matches the type of popup being triggered (e.g., aria-haspopup="menu" or aria-haspopup="dialog").

info.what: Highlights visual grouping containers (<fieldset>) and their titles (<legend>).
info.why: Crucial for grouping related radio buttons or complex form sections to give screen readers proper structural context. WCAG 1.3.1: Info and Relationships
info.fix: Verify that every <fieldset> has a descriptive <legend> as its very first child element.

info.what: Flags elements that receive keyboard focus but are hidden from Assistive Technologies via aria-hidden='true'.
info.why: Keyboard users can reach them, but screen readers cannot, creating a severe operational mismatch and invisible focus traps. WCAG 4.1.2: Name, Role, Value
info.fix: If the element is part of a hidden dialog or closed menu, set it to tabindex="-1" or use the inert attribute on its container. Alternatively, remove aria-hidden="true" if the control should be active.

info.what: Flags skipped sequential levels (e.g., jumping from H1 directly to H3) or fake structural classes imitating headings. Note: Starting a page directly with an H2 is not flagged as a skipped level.
info.why: Headings map the document's structure. Skipping levels breaks the outline and deeply confuses screen reader navigation. WCAG 1.3.1: Info and Relationships
info.fix: Ensure headings increment by only one level at a time (e.g., an H2 should only be followed by an H2 or H3). Use proper native heading tags (<h1> - <h6>) instead of styling generic <div> elements to look like headings.
info.detection_note: Skipped levels are exact. 'Fake headings' are guessed from class names containing 'heading' or 'title' plus short text, so some results may be false positives.

info.what: Flags elements dynamically injected with a tabindex > 0.
info.why: Overrides natural DOM focus order, creating unpredictable and confusing navigation paths for screen readers and keyboard users. WCAG 2.4.3: Focus Order
info.fix: Remove the positive tabindex value. Rely on the natural DOM order by physically rearranging HTML elements, or use tabindex="0" to safely add custom elements to the focus flow.

info.what: Maps mandatory inputs enforced via HTML5 required or aria-required.
info.why: Ensures required status is programmatically available, not just visually styled. WCAG 3.3.1: Error Identification
info.fix: Verify that the programmatic requirement matches the visual cue (e.g., an asterisk). Avoid using aria-required="false", simply omit the attribute if the field is optional.

info.what: Flags elements explicitly marked with aria-invalid='true'.
info.why: Identifies application-enforced validation errors. Used to ensure visual error styling is programmatically communicated to screen reader users. WCAG 3.3.1: Error Identification
info.fix: Ensure an accessible error message is actively linked to the invalid field using aria-errormessage="id" or aria-describedby="id" so the user knows how to correct it.
